text:
matt: FYI we're seeing a 12-18% p50 latency bump on 8k workloads after yesterday's kernel autotune rollout. looks correlated with seqlen bucketing changes.
anna: saw that in the perf dashboard too. perf/regressions shows spike starting ~1748883000. logs point to prefill choosing decode path kernels for short-prefill buckets. :thinking: 
jess: can you paste the benchmark snippet? which model and device?
matt: gpt-medium-ish on H100s, batch=16, seqs mostly ~64-512 (heavy tail). autotune picked fused-fwd kernels for decode path when seqlen threshold was 96; prefill still routed to the old prefill kernels. ends up with extra memcpy and kv-cache realignment.
anna: here's a small extract from the profile (truncated):
```
Profile summary: prefill_step: 34ms -> 92ms
- kernel_launch: fused_attn_v2 (decode) increased by 2.6x
- kv_repack memcpy: 18ms
- cache_miss_evictions: +23/min
```
liam: so sounds like mismatch in path selection: autotune threshold moves boundary -> some inputs switch to decode-optimized kernels but prefill pipeline didn't switch allocator/pack layout. That causes repack penalty.
jess: we added a lightweight sentinel that picks kernel family by "route_id" earlier in the stack to avoid repacks. maybe sentinel wasn't rolled.
matt: exact. sentinel flag = enable_route_family_lock. disabled in canary. enabling on canary nodes removed memcpys and latency returned to baseline.
anna: quick mitigation: add hysteresis to seqlen bucketing -> don't flip route until two consecutive batches cross threshold. reduces oscillation. also add explicit KV layout compatibility check before switching.
liam: +1. we should also add a cheap fingerprint of KV layout into the routing key so prefill/decoder routing agree. cheap hash of dims + quantization bits.
jess: for immediate patch I'll push a conservative threshold update and enable route_family_lock for all H100 canaries. test plan: run perf-runner workload with synthetic long-tail and real traffic replay.
matt: sounds good. do we need a rollback path?
anna: create a deploy flag to force prefill->decode mapping to "legacy" if we detect >5% memcopy overhead during warmup. fallback should be immediate and circuit-breaker style.
liam: I'll open a PR with hysteresis + routing hash. small change: 6 lines in routing_policy.cc. will tag you all for review.
jess: infra-bot ran a quick microbench on canary after enabling route_family_lock:
```
infra-bot: microbench results: canary-group-a (H100): p50 28ms -> 24ms, p95 110ms -> 95ms, memcpy bytes down 42%
```
anna: nice. we should keep an eye on tail though; sometimes batching heuristics increase p99.
matt: agree. also need to update autotune docs: warn about kernel family compatibility across prefill/decode. could add a post-tuning check that simulates prefill->decode transitions.
jess: note for changelog: "autotune: add route_family_lock and seqlen hysteresis to prevent KV repack thrashing".
liam: timeline: patch PR today, canary by EOD, monitor for 48h. I'll add alerts for memcpy growth and kv-evictions.
matt: thanks. if anyone sees nontrivial regression after enabling, ping me and we'll revert the autotune rollout. :eyes:
anna: cc @infra-bot can you keep hourly aggregate logs for the next 72h and post the memcopy/gc metrics to the thread?
infra-bot: ack. posting hourly summary to this thread. next post in 1h. :robot_face:
jess: one more thought — we should add a small unit test in runtime/test that ensures kernel_family(schema_a) == kernel_family(schema_b) for transitions expected in rollout. catches these mismatches earlier.
matt: agreed. ok let's move. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
